gaps.sentence: They're building ___ new library near the town hall.
gaps.explanation: A new library — first mention; the town hall is the known one.

gaps.sentence: She goes to ___ school by bus every morning.
gaps.explanation: 'Go to school/work/bed/church' (as participant) takes no article.

gaps.sentence: I'd like ___ orange juice, please — small or large?
gaps.explanation: Drinks offered as an amount take 'some' (or no article): some orange juice.

gaps.sentence: Mount Everest is ___ highest mountain in the world.
He was ___ last person to leave the building.
gaps.explanation: Ordinals take 'the': the last person, the first time.

gaps.sentence: He had ___ operation on his knee last year.
gaps.explanation: 'Operation' starts with a vowel sound, so 'an operation'.

gaps.sentence: ___ Hyde Park is lovely in autumn.
gaps.explanation: Most park names take no article: Hyde Park, Central Park (exception: the Grands Boulevards style names).
'The + nationality adjective' = the people as a group: the French, the British.
